# OMP002 `accumulation-without-reduction`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A shared scalar is accumulated inside an OpenMP parallel region without `reduction`.

## Why

`s = s + x(i)` in a parallel loop reads and writes the shared `s` from every thread: updates are
lost and the result changes from run to run. A `reduction(+:s)` clause gives each thread a private
partial sum and combines them at the end of the region; `atomic` is correct but serialises every
update.

## Reported

```fortran
!$omp parallel do
do i = 1, n
  s = s + x(i)
end do
```

## Preferred

```fortran
!$omp parallel do reduction(+:s)
do i = 1, n
  s = s + x(i)
end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OMP002] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OMP002` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
